sections.label: B
sections.title: Complete the sentences.
sections.note: Use the Unit 15 vocabulary that best fits each context.

questions.prompt: 1. There isn't a lot of rain falling, just a few ___.
questions.explanation: Raindrops are individual drops of rain.

questions.prompt: 2. The mud and rocks from the ___ on the mountain knocked down many trees.
questions.explanation: A landslide is a mass of rock and earth moving down a slope.

questions.prompt: 3. It takes a lot of ___ to work together to repair a town after a bad storm.
questions.explanation: Teamwork is the combined effort of people working toward the same goal.

questions.prompt: 4. The ten ___ of the storm were brought to the hospital.
questions.explanation: Victims are people who are harmed by an accident or disaster.

sections.label: D
sections.title: Look and write questions. Use the present perfect and ever.
sections.note: Use Has with a singular third-person subject and Have with you or plural subjects.

questions.prompt: 1. he / drive / in thunderstorms
answers: Has he ever driven in thunderstorms
questions.explanation: Use Has + he + ever + past participle driven.

questions.prompt: 2. tornadoes / happen / in your town
answers: Have tornadoes ever happened in your town
Have tornados ever happened in your town
questions.explanation: Tornadoes is plural, so use Have; happened is the past participle of happen.

questions.prompt: 3. you / be / in an earthquake
answers: Have you ever been in an earthquake
questions.explanation: Use Have + you + ever + past participle been.

questions.prompt: 4. this desert / have / snow
answers: Has this desert ever had snow
questions.explanation: This desert is singular, so use Has; had is the past participle of have.

sections.label: E
sections.title: Complete the sentences. Write Has or Have.
sections.note: Choose the auxiliary that agrees with the subject.

questions.prompt: 1. ___ you ever been in a flood?
questions.explanation: You takes Have in a present-perfect question.

questions.prompt: 2. ___ she ever experienced a tornado?
questions.explanation: She is third-person singular, so use Has.

questions.prompt: 3. ___ you ever learned about thunderstorms?
questions.explanation: You takes Have.

questions.prompt: 4. ___ they ever felt an earthquake?
questions.explanation: They is plural, so use Have.

sections.label: F
sections.title: Write the words in the correct order. Then listen and write the answers.
sections.note: First make the present-perfect question. Then play the audio and write the short answer.

questions.prompt: 1. seen / ever / a / you / Have / tornado

parts.label: Question
answers: Have you ever seen a tornado
parts.explanation: Use Have + you + ever + past participle seen.

parts.label: Listening answer
parts.explanation: The speaker answers negatively: No, I haven't.

questions.prompt: 2. office / worked / an / Have / ever / in / you

parts.label: Question
answers: Have you ever worked in an office
parts.explanation: Use Have + you + ever + past participle worked + place.

parts.label: Listening answer
parts.explanation: The speaker answers positively: Yes, I have.

questions.prompt: 3. snow / ever / home / Have / because / you / of / stayed

parts.label: Question
answers: Have you ever stayed home because of snow
parts.explanation: Use Have + you + ever + past participle stayed, followed by the reason.

parts.label: Listening answer
parts.explanation: The speaker answers negatively: No, I haven't.

sections.label: J
sections.title: Complete the sentences. Write yet, just, or already.
sections.note: Use just for something very recent, yet in questions and negatives, and already for something completed earlier than expected.

questions.prompt: 1. He has ___ got cash from the ATM. I saw him at the machine a few minutes ago.
questions.explanation: A few minutes ago indicates a very recent action, so use just.

questions.prompt: 2. Have you asked your teacher about the test ___?
questions.explanation: Yet commonly appears at the end of a present-perfect question.

questions.prompt: 3. They've ___ come home from the supermarket. They arrived five minutes ago.
questions.explanation: Điền just. Tách mốc five minutes ago sang câu quá khứ đơn để không ghép sai với hiện tại hoàn thành.

questions.prompt: 4. He hasn't used his new computer ___.
questions.explanation: Yet appears at the end of a negative present-perfect sentence.

questions.prompt: 5. I've ___ read that book five times!
questions.explanation: Already emphasizes that the action has been completed repeatedly before now.

sections.label: K
sections.title: Circle the correct words.
sections.note: Choose the word that occupies the correct position and expresses the intended time relationship.

questions.prompt: 1. Have you called your mother ___?
questions.explanation: Yet is used at the end of a present-perfect question.

questions.prompt: 2. I've ___ finished my homework.
questions.explanation: Just goes between have and the past participle to describe a recent action.

questions.prompt: 3. My mom has ___ left for work.
questions.explanation: Already fits an affirmative present-perfect statement.

questions.prompt: 4. We haven't learned about tornadoes ___.
questions.explanation: Yet is used at the end of a negative present-perfect sentence.

questions.prompt: 5. Have you ___ finished watching the movie?
questions.explanation: Just can be placed before finished to ask whether the action happened moments ago.

sections.label: L
sections.title: Look and write sentences. Use the present perfect.
sections.note: Place just, already, or yet in the correct position and use the past participle.

questions.prompt: 1. He / already get cash / from the ATM
answers: He has already gotten cash from the ATM
He has already got cash from the ATM
questions.explanation: Use has + already + past participle. Gotten is standard American English; got is also accepted in British English.

questions.prompt: 2. She / just eat / lunch
questions.explanation: Use has + just + past participle eaten.

questions.prompt: 3. The hurricane / not make landfall / yet
answers: The hurricane has not made landfall yet
The hurricane hasn't made landfall yet
questions.explanation: Use has not + past participle made, with yet at the end.

questions.prompt: 4. I / just buy / the first-aid kit
answers: I have just bought the first-aid kit
I have just bought the first aid kit
questions.explanation: Use have + just + past participle bought.
